title: Bot personality nuance — situational personality shifts, player-movement anticipation, bait + bluff behaviours
intent: Bots currently use STATIC danger maps + STATIC personality weights — same behaviour Round 1, Round 5, leading vs losing. Real opponents anticipate player moves, switch playstyles when winning/losing, occasionally bait + bluff. This story adds three layers of nuance: (1) PLAYER ANTICIPATION — track player's last 3 moves, predict next cell, factor into danger / bomb-place / chase decisions. (2) SITUATIONAL PERSONALITY SHIFTS — Coward becomes slightly aggressive when leading 2-0; Hunter becomes cautious when behind 0-2; Miner ignores combat until forced. (3) BAIT + BLUFF — Hunter occasionally pretends to flee then turns around to bomb; Coward places a non-threatening bomb in plain sight (psychological), keeping the real threat hidden. Each layer makes bots READ DIFFERENTLY across rounds, not as 'walking + bombing'.
rationale: Source: bot AI feels mechanical despite 9 power-ups (pre-GDP-029-009). After 029-009 tactical use lands, bots have RICH verb space but still static behaviour. This story is the personality-evolution layer — bots evolve within a session. Marked `could` because the base verb-execution from 029-009 is the bigger win; this is the polish on top. Cost ~150 LOC + careful tuning. Risk: anticipation can feel cheap if too accurate; tuning matters.
acceptanceHints: DEPENDS ON: GDP-2026-05-29-009 (bot tactical power-up usage). This layer extends the bot decision process with predictive + adaptive elements.
LAYER 1 — PLAYER ANTICIPATION (track + predict player position):
Bot AI gains per-tracker state: { recentPlayerCells: Cell[], lastObservedAt: number }.
Per fixedUpdate, append player's current cell to recentPlayerCells (keep last 5).

predictNextPlayerCell(): if last 3 cells form a straight line in direction D, predict next cell in D. Otherwise predict current cell + queuedDirection from playerInput observation (if Hunter can 'see' it).
Use predicted cell in: bomb-place decisions (place bomb where player will be, not where they ARE) + chase pathing (move toward predicted cell, not current).
Per personality:
Hunter: heavily weights predicted cell for bomb-place + chase.
Coward: uses predicted cell for FLEE direction — flees away from where player WILL BE.
Miner: ignores anticipation (focused on soft blocks).
Decay: if last observed > 5 seconds ago, anticipation confidence drops to 0 (player out of sight).
LAYER 2 — SITUATIONAL PERSONALITY SHIFTS (round-to-round adaptation):
Bot AI reads RoundState.tally to detect winning/losing trend across the current match.
Shift trigger when tally diff is significant (player leading +2, bot leading +2, etc.):
Coward → 'Brave Coward' when bot is leading 2-0 in match: aggression weight +0.15, dash chase enabled rarely. Visual: takes more risks because comfortably ahead.
Coward → 'Pure Coward' when behind 0-2: aggression weight -0.10, shield-protected risk-taking off (too late to take chances).
Hunter → 'Patient Hunter' when behind 0-2: aggression weight -0.10, more careful bomb placement. Visual: stops rushing.
Hunter → 'Reckless Hunter' when leading 2-0: aggression +0.20, more bomb-place near player. Visual: aggressive finisher.
Miner → 'Combat Miner' when behind 0-2: aggression +0.20 (panic combat), shifts focus from blocks to player.
Miner → 'Pure Miner' when leading 2-0: aggression -0.10, full miner mode (collecting pickups, ignoring player).
Shifts persist throughout the round + reset when match resolves.
HUD telegraph: small icon next to bot's tally entry shows shifted state (e.g. '🔥' for reckless, '🛡' for patient). Player can READ the shift.
LAYER 3 — BAIT + BLUFF (psychological play):
Per personality, probability of bluff per round:
Hunter: 10% probability per round of executing 'fake flee' — flees from player, gets within bomb range from opposite direction, places bomb. Visible misdirection.

Coward: 15% probability of placing a 'decoy bomb' in plain sight (a fuse-throw bomb that detonates harmlessly far from anyone — fake threat to occupy player's attention), then placing the REAL trap bomb elsewhere.
Miner: 5% probability of pretending to be cornered, then walking past player to a soft-block-rich area. Subtle.
Bluffs don't fire more than once per round per bot (don't spam).
Bluff outcomes deterministic — seeded by (bot entity id + round number + scene seed).
INTERACTION WITH MULTI-BOT SOLO (S141 — 3 bots):
In multi-bot mode, each bot personality + state independent. Anticipation tracks the LOCAL PLAYER for each bot (not other bots).
Personality shifts: each bot independently shifts based on its own player-bot tally (well-defined in multi-bot since each bot has its own kill count vs player).
Bluffs: each bot bluffs independently. Can lead to amusing emergent coordination (Coward bluffs while Hunter actually attacks).
INTERACTION WITH MULTIPLAYER (server-authoritative from S125):
Server-side bot-ai runs same anticipation + shifts + bluffs logic. Determinism per server-tick.
Player anticipation: server's bot tracks server-known player cells.
DECISION COMPOSITION (extends 029-009):
1. Compute danger map.
2. Compute opportunity map per power-up.
3. APPLY shifted personality weights (Layer 2).
4. APPLY anticipation predictions to position decisions (Layer 1).
5. Check for bluff opportunity (Layer 3) — if bluff triggers this tick, override action.
6. Pick highest-scoring action.
DETERMINISM: all layers seeded by (bot id + round number + scene seed + fixedUpdate tick). Bot-vs-bot regression continues to resolve.
BALANCE / TUNING:
Anticipation must NOT be perfect — 100% correct prediction is too punishing. Tune predictNextPlayerCell() to ~60% accuracy (sometimes guesses wrong) by adding 30% random jitter.
Shifts must be GRADUAL — clamp aggression delta to ±0.20 max from baseline. Avoid wild personality swings.
Bluffs must be RARE (5-15% probability) — too common and they become predictable.
TESTS:
Hunter bot anticipates player moving E for 3 ticks → places bomb at predicted+1 cell.
Coward leading 2-0 → aggression weight +0.15 vs base.
Reckless Hunter places bombs at distance-1 to player (where baseline Hunter would place distance-2).
Hunter bluff at 10% probability across 100 simulated rounds → ~10 bluffs observed.
Bluff outcome deterministic per (bot id, round, seed).
Anticipation decays after 5s of no player observation.
Multi-bot solo with 3 personalities → each shifts independently per its own tally.
VISUAL QA:
Round 1, Hunter at baseline aggression — looks like Hunter (chases + bombs).
Round 3, Hunter leading 2-0 — Reckless Hunter, visibly more aggressive bomb placement near player. HUD icon shows shift state.
Round 3, Hunter behind 0-2 — Patient Hunter, more cautious. Player can READ the change.
Bluff scenario: Hunter fakes flee, player chases, Hunter loops back + bombs from opposite. Player feels '!' moment.
Anticipation: bot bombs cell where player is HEADED, not where player IS — feels intelligent.

OUT OF SCOPE:
Learning across sessions (bots remember player from previous games). Per-round only.
Bot vs bot bait + bluff (only player-targeted).
Visual emote animations on bluff (bot looking puzzled etc.). Decision-only.
Personality switching mid-round (one shift per round, locked at round start).
Difficulty preset interaction beyond existing aggression/reaction modifiers.
Bot taunts via voice synth (e.g. mocking laugh on bait success). Audio stays uniform per existing voice-synth GDPs.
